<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Coarse fallback — **27** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c8c803c293af7fdcba18b142e64ee9ce80bfc198` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c6c4351a82ec2c6e3ee9428d8949fbcea0b86388`
Local-runs: none

Read-only, against the head above (3 commits: `030a795001` code, `77e21f89c2` changeset, `c6c4351a82` the note correction; merge base with `main` `16096e8d7b`; `origin/main` read at `0ef9029da4`). Inputs: card #22335 (body and every comment: 6068196632, 6070759640, 6071726795, 6072413112, 6072671511); #22286, landed PR #22334 and its pending note on `main`; #5274; PR #22354 (landed on `main` as `f6e1d49e90` while this PR sat open); this PR's body, 5-file list and net diff against the merge base; `lifecycle.mdx` and `events.mdx` on `main`; the head's check-runs. Nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Public surface: none added — right.** `ObjectKernelConfig` keeps `gracefulShutdown?: boolean` (kernel.ts:97); the diff to the declaration is JSDoc only. No key, option, export or type moves. Not C.
- **The accept-set change is one predicate — right.** The genuine-timeout branch (still entered only by the identity-matched `shutdownTimeoutError`) now reads `this.config.gracefulShutdown` (kernel.ts:626), the same truthiness test the constructor uses to install the listeners (kernel.ts:265). That is the ruling's intent ("the kernel installed the signal listeners itself"): a kernel exits on a timeout exactly when it took the signals. The declared deviation from `=== false` is right: an explicit `gracefulShutdown: undefined` overrides the spread default and reads the same on both halves (no listeners, no exit), consistent by construction, whereas `=== false` would exit a kernel that installed nothing. No producer passes `undefined` or a computed value: a PCRE grep on the head over `packages/**`, `apps/**`, `examples/**`, `scripts/**` for any non-literal value finds 0 lines (positive control on the new test file hits).
- **The `true` path, byte-for-byte — confirmed.** Inside the new `if` the three statements are the old ones unchanged: `this.logger.error('Shutdown timed out — forcing exit', error as Error)`, `await this.logger.destroy()`, `process.exit(1)`. The diff has exactly two hunks in kernel.ts (the JSDoc and this branch); `handleShutdownSignal`, `registerShutdownSignals`, `releaseShutdownSignals`, `performShutdown`, the non-timeout branch and the `finally` are untouched.
- **The `false` path — matches B.** State is set `stopped` (kernel.ts:616) and listeners released (617, a no-op for `false`) before the branch; the else branch logs once at `error` with the `Error`, falls through to `finally` (`logger.destroy()`), and `shutdown()` resolves. The only `process.exit` sites a core kernel can reach are kernel.ts:634 (inside the `true` guard) and `safeExit` at 1023/1026 (the signal handler, reached only from listeners a `false` kernel never installs), so a `false` kernel never ends the process. The catch has no rethrow and `destroy()` has no reject path: `shutdown()` still never rejects. Not D.
- **The new log line — right.** It names the timeout in ms, that the teardown is still running in the background and may hold what it has not released, that `gracefulShutdown` is false, that the process is NOT being exited, and that the host decides. No tracker number in the runtime string.
- **JSDoc — right.** Both meanings (who installs the listeners; who exits on a timeout), the hung teardown not cancelled, when to set `false`, and that `shutdown()` never rejects under either setting.
- **M4, the abandoned teardown — confirmed, and the pin is real.** `performShutdown()` (kernel.ts:935-962) writes no `state` (all six `this.state =` sites are in `bootstrap()`/`shutdown()`), releases no listener (the three `releaseShutdownSignals()` calls are at 559, 613, 617), and its only effects are plugin `destroy()` calls and `shutdownHandlers`, each in its own try/catch. `raceWithTimeout` is `Promise.race([operation, guard.expiry])`, so the operation keeps a subscriber and a later rejection is handled. Lines it logs after `logger.destroy()` reach the console only (`fileStream` cleared at logger.ts:482; `write` guards on it at 396). The first new test releases the gate after `shutdown()` resolved, `vi.waitFor`s `['teardown-resumed', 'destroy']` (fails on timeout, so not vacuous), then asserts `stopped`, a no-op second `shutdown()`, and `exit` never called.
- **The #5274 pin — subject kept.** Same title, same three assertions (`Shutdown timed out — forcing exit` logged, `exit` called with 1, `stopped`); the fixture moves to `gracefulShutdown: true`; the `finally` removes any listener added beyond the pre-test set (the kernel also releases its own at `stopped`). Nothing weakened.
- **The new file, 4 tests — tests the subject.** (1) `false` plus a genuine timeout: resolves, no exit, `stopped`, exactly one error-level timeout line carrying an `Error`, no `forcing exit` line, teardown abandoned then released as above; (2) R7's shape: two `false` kernels, stopping the hung one leaves the sibling `running` with no exit, and the sibling still stops; (3)(4) controls under `false`: a throwing `destroy()` (isolated inside the teardown) and an error escaping `performShutdown` (the non-timeout branch) — neither exits, neither is reported as a timeout.
- **Ablation partition — consistent with the code.** Leg A (`if (true)`) reds exactly the two tests that assert no exit on a timeout; the controls never reach the timeout branch and the #5274 pin expects the exit. Leg B (`if (false)`) reds only the #5274 pin; the `false` tests pass either way, and the reported message (one error line present, not the `forcing exit` text) is what the else branch produces.
- **M2, who relied on the exit — confirmed on the head.** `gracefulShutdown: false` matches 50 files on the head (49 on `main` plus the new test), 0 non-test lines; `packages/cli`, `packages/runtime/src`, `packages/objectql/src` and `packages/verify/src` mention `gracefulShutdown` nowhere outside tests. The production kernels take the default: `serve.ts:3173` `new Runtime({ kernel: { logger }, cluster })`; `schema-migrate.ts:492` `new Runtime({ cluster: false })` (the only two constructions in `packages/cli/src`); `runtime.ts:78` forwards `config.kernel` without setting it; `kernel-factory.ts:35` and `harness.ts:504` `new ObjectKernel()`. The cloud host's behaviour after `shutdown()` returns is NOT MEASURED (no read access) — the changeset's remedy is conditional ("A host that sets `gracefulShutdown: false` ... and relied on that exit") and restates the option's contract ("already handles the signals itself"), not the cloud code's current behaviour. Right.
- **Docs.** `lifecycle.mdx` 826-829 ("otherwise it stays out of the process-management business") was false only on the timeout path and is now true: a `false` kernel calls no exit anywhere. Its "[6] Exit process" diagram sits under "SIGTERM received", the signal path, unchanged. `events.mdx:39` ("`process.exit(1)` is reserved for a genuine `shutdownTimeout` overrun") is still true as the exclusivity statement it is — the exit happens in no other case — and is now incomplete, not false: it does not say the overrun exits only under `gracefulShutdown: true`. Not this PR's page (`domain:devx`); the one-clause qualification, for whoever owns it: "— and, since #22335, only under `gracefulShutdown: true`; a `gracefulShutdown: false` kernel returns to its host instead". Noted, no FAIL.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/22335-graceful-shutdown-false-no-exit.md`: `'@objectstack/core': minor`, title `fix(core)!:`, the **BREAKING** banner, ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. **Level right.** A host may rely on the old exit, so the change is breaking; under the launch-window convention (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`) a breaking change ships `minor` with the banner — `patch` would under-grade it and `major` is refused. `Check Changeset` steps 11, 13 and 15 (changeset present; ADR-0087 disposition present; no major) are green on the head.
- **ADR-0087 disposition right.** No spec key, authorable spelling, export, option, type or stored shape moves, so `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to rewrite; the body carries no FROM/TO rewrite (no migration heading, arrow or table), so `no-migration-prescription` is honest; `runtime-interface-only` needs a named exported declaration that moves, and none does.
- **Every sentence true against the diff and `main`:** the `false` behaviour and the uncancelled teardown (the else branch); the docs sentence it cites (`lifecycle.mdx:826-829`); "the timeout branch did not read the option" (base `kernel.ts`); the `true` path's log line and exit; a throwing teardown never exits under either setting (the non-timeout branch, #5274); `shutdown()` never rejects; nothing added; every CLI kernel takes the default (the two constructions above); `shutdown()` returns at the timer whether or not the teardown finished, and a hung teardown "can" keep the loop alive. No sentence says pre mode is absent; `.changeset/pre.json` is untouched by the diff.
- **`Clause-②: no` — confirmed** in the changeset, the PR body and the claim (6071726795): no key, export or option is added.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions` is `[]` in both reports. Every declared deviation and out-of-scope finding, answered:

- Predicate truthiness instead of `=== false` — right, see ①.
- Two controls instead of one — accepted; the escaping-error control is the one catch branch no existing test reached.
- M2's cloud half NOT MEASURED — accepted; the ruling itself named that host, and the changeset's wording is conditional (①).
- Core suite ran without the `--maxWorkers=2` cap (bare `--`) — a local-run detail; `Test Core` on the head is the gate, and it is green.
- PR body stale (round 0) — the body stored on the head now carries the corrected Tests heading, the measured `dual-build-cjs-loads` reading and the "Patch round 1" section; current.
- The 22286 note not edited (round 0) — superseded by patch round 1, judged below.
- Labeler-added labels (`documentation`, `size/m`, `tests`, `tooling`) — no bearing.
- Worktree recreated; no MCP call in round 1 — no bearing.
- `events.mdx:39` — still true, incomplete; answered in ① with the clause; no carrier needed.
- Explicit `gracefulShutdown: undefined` — consistent by construction; no producer passes it (①).
- No return-value signal for a timeout — by the ruling (D not taken); the host reads the `error` line; accepted, no card.
- A child logger writing after a `false` timeout — read, not measured, and read again here: children share the opener's stream (logger.ts:472) and the parent ends it in `destroy()` (480-489); a later child write trips the stream's `error` handler, which disables file logging with one notice. Pre-existing on every normal `shutdown()` completion as well; not this PR's; no card.

#### The deliberate correction of `.changeset/22286-kernel-signal-listeners.md` — confirmed

- `.changeset/pre.json` on `main` is `{ "mode": "pre", "tag": "next" }` and nothing else — no consumed list. The 22286 note is on `main` (blob `c91c506d19`), not in `packages/core/CHANGELOG.md` (0 hits); core is at 17.7.0 with 151 pending notes. Both notes ship in the same release.
- Before: "A genuine shutdown timeout still calls `process.exit(1)`."
- After: "With `gracefulShutdown: true`, a genuine shutdown timeout still calls `process.exit(1)`; a `gracefulShutdown: false` kernel no longer exits (#22335)."
- Sentence by sentence: the old sentence is unconditional and becomes false once this PR lands (a `false` kernel's genuine timeout no longer exits). The new first clause is true against the diff (the exit sits inside the `true` guard); the new second clause is true (the else branch); the citation names the card. Nothing else in that note changes: `git diff` on the file is one line, +1/−1 at line 12 (`c91c506d19..a0d0a3b23e`).
- So `Check Changeset` red on this head is deliberate and this record confirms it. Its failing step is 12, `check-empty-changeset.mjs` (the foreign-changeset rule refuses a note present on the merge base and changed by the PR); steps 11, 13 and 15 are green. Not a required context.

#### The merge with #22354

#22354 landed on `main` as `f6e1d49e90` after this PR opened; this branch is not merged with `main` (merge base `16096e8d7b`; CI ran on the merge with base `c8c803c293`). `git merge-tree --write-tree 0ef9029da4 c6c4351a82` exits 0 (tree `c4198761e0`); none of the five touched paths carries a `merge` attribute (`git check-attr`), so the locally registered os-regen driver plays no part and this is the plain text merge GitHub runs; GitHub reports `mergeable: true`. The merged `kernel.ts` carries both changes intact: `bootPhaseHooks` (config, `bootstrap()`, the withheld-hooks warn) and the new timeout branch, and it differs from this head's `kernel.ts` only by #22354's hunks. The regions do not interact: #22354's test fixture is `gracefulShutdown: false` with a completing teardown and asserts `stopped` with no exit, unchanged under this PR. The queue's rebuilt generation runs the required set on the joint tree.
